title: Problem 1
statement_text: Let $p\geq 1$ be a fixed rational number. Instance: A (multi-)digraph $D$. Decide whether $\vec{\chi}^{\ast}(D)\leq p$.
context_text: The problem of determining the complexity of deciding whether the star dichromatic number of a digraph is at most $p$ was posed by Hochstättler and Steiner (2019). For $p=1$ the problem reduces to deciding acyclicity, solvable in linear time; the hardness for $p>1$ was left open.
paper_contribution: Proves NP-completeness for every fixed rational $p>1$, fully resolving the open problem.
paper_title: On the Complexity of Digraph Colourings and Vertex Arboricity

title: Problem 2.15
statement_text: Let $F$ be a fixed (multi-)digraph. Instance: A (multi-)digraph $D$. Decide whether $D$ is circularly $F$-colourable.
context_text: Digraphs are loopless but may have parallel and anti-parallel arcs; a digon is a directed cycle of length two, and a vertex set is acyclic if it induces an acyclic subdigraph. A circular homomorphism from a digraph $D_1$ to a digraph $D_2$ is a map $\phi:V(D_1)\to V(D_2)$ such that the preimage of every acyclic set of $D_2$ is acyclic in $D_1$; equivalently, for every directed cycle $C$ of $D_1$, $D_2[\phi(V(C))]$ contains a directed cycle. For symmetric digraphs (each edge replaced by a digon) these are exactly graph homomorphisms, and acyclic homomorphisms are a special case. A digraph $D$ is circularly $F$-colourable if there is a circular homomorphism from $D$ to $F$. An acyclic $(k,d)$-colouring of $D$ is a map $c:V(D)\to\mathbb{Z}_k$ such that for every $i$ the preimage of the cyclic interval $\{i,\dots,i+d-1\}$ is acyclic, and the star dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}^{*}(D)$ is the infimum of $k/d$ over such colourings; $\vec{\chi}^{*}(D)\le k/d$ if and only if $D$ is circularly $\vec{C}(k,d)$-colourable, where $\vec{C}(k,d)$ has vertex set $\mathbb{Z}_k$ and an arc $(i,j)$ whenever $(j-i)\bmod k\ge d$. The problem, a directed analogue of the $H$-colouring problem for graphs, is to determine for which fixed $F$ this decision problem is polynomial and for which it is NP-complete. It generalises the question, posed by Hochstättler, of the complexity of deciding $\vec{\chi}^{*}(D)\le p$, which the authors prove NP-complete for every rational $p>1$. If $F$ is acyclic only acyclic digraphs map circularly to $F$, so the problem is polynomial; the authors conjecture that it is NP-complete whenever $F$ contains a directed cycle, and prove this when $F$ is digon-free, or the symmetric part of $F$ (the graph of its digons) contains an odd cycle, or $F$ is 2-colourable (dichromatic number at most $2$).
notes: The complete dichotomy (all F with a directed cycle) is conjectured but not fully proved within the paper.
paper_title: On the Complexity of Digraph Colourings and Vertex Arboricity

title: Conjecture 2.16
statement_text: Let $F$ be a digraph which contains a directed cycle. Then the circular $F$-colouring problem is NP-complete.
context_text: Digraphs are loopless but may have parallel and anti-parallel arcs; a digon is a directed cycle of length two, and a vertex set is acyclic if it induces an acyclic subdigraph. A circular homomorphism from a digraph $D_1$ to a digraph $D_2$ is a map $\phi:V(D_1)\to V(D_2)$ such that the preimage of every acyclic set of $D_2$ is acyclic in $D_1$; equivalently, for every directed cycle $C$ of $D_1$, $D_2[\phi(V(C))]$ contains a directed cycle. For symmetric digraphs (each edge replaced by a digon) these are exactly graph homomorphisms, and acyclic homomorphisms are a special case. A digraph $D$ is circularly $F$-colourable if there is a circular homomorphism from $D$ to $F$. The circular $F$-colouring problem asks, for a fixed digraph $F$, whether an input (multi-)digraph is circularly $F$-colourable; it is a directed analogue of the $H$-colouring problem, and for $F=\vec{C}(k,d)$ (vertex set $\mathbb{Z}_k$, arc $(i,j)$ whenever $(j-i)\bmod k\ge d$) it amounts to deciding whether the star dichromatic number is at most $k/d$. If $F$ is acyclic, only acyclic digraphs map circularly to $F$, so the problem is polynomial; the conjecture says that, assuming P$\ne$NP, these are the only polynomial cases. The authors prove it when $F$ is digon-free, or the symmetric part of $F$ (the graph on $V(F)$ whose edges are the digons) contains an odd cycle, or $F$ is 2-colourable (dichromatic number at most $2$); this parallels the classification of Feder et al. for acyclic homomorphisms.
paper_title: On the Complexity of Digraph Colourings and Vertex Arboricity

title: Problem 3.21
statement_text: Let $p\geq 1$ be a fixed real number. Instance: A (multi-)digraph $D$. Decide whether $\vec{\chi}_{f}(D)\leq p$.
context_text: Digraphs are loopless but may have parallel and anti-parallel arcs; a digon is a directed cycle of length two, and a vertex set is acyclic if it induces an acyclic subdigraph. For a digraph $D$, let $\mathcal{A}(D)$ be the family of acyclic vertex sets and $\mathcal{A}(D,v)$ those containing $v$; the fractional dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}_f(D)$ is the minimum of $\sum_{A\in\mathcal{A}(D)}x_A$ subject to $\sum_{A\in\mathcal{A}(D,v)}x_A\ge1$ for every vertex $v$ and $x\ge0$ (equivalently, the minimum $k/b$ such that each vertex can be assigned $b$ colours out of $k$ with every colour class acyclic). For $p=1$ the problem is equivalent to acyclicity, hence polynomial, and it is in NP for every $p$. The paper proves that it is NP-complete for every real $p>1$ with $p\ne2$, mirroring results of Feder et al. for the circular dichromatic number; thus only the case $p=2$ remains open, and the authors strongly believe it is also NP-complete.
notes: The case $p=2$ remains unresolved after this paper.
paper_title: On the Complexity of Digraph Colourings and Vertex Arboricity

title: Conjecture 5.38 (Jaeger)
statement_text: Any planar graph $G$ of girth at least $4k$ admits a homomorphism to $C_{2k+1}$. In other words, $\chi_{c}(G)\leq\frac{2k+1}{k}$.
context_text: This well-known conjecture on homomorphism bounds for planar graphs of large girth is attributed to Jaeger (1984). It contains as a special case for $k=1$ Grötzsch's theorem that every triangle-free planar graph is 3-colourable. The paper cites it as motivation for the directed analogue Conjecture 5.39.
paper_contribution: Mentions the conjecture as direct motivation for posing a directed analogue (Conjecture 5.39) in the framework of circular homomorphisms between digraphs; no new progress on the conjecture itself is claimed.
paper_title: On the Complexity of Digraph Colourings and Vertex Arboricity

title: Conjecture 5.39
statement_text: Any planar digraph $D$ of directed girth at least $k\geq 3$ admits a circular homomorphism to $\vec{C}_{k-1}$. In other words, $\vec{\chi}^{\ast}(D)\leq\frac{k-1}{k-2}$.
context_text: Posed by Hochstättler and Steiner (2019) as a directed analogue of Jaeger's conjecture for graphs. The case $k=3$ corresponds to the 2-Colour-Conjecture of Neumann-Lara, and $k=4$ gives a directed analogue of Grötzsch's theorem for oriented planar $\vec{C}_{3}$-free digraphs.
paper_contribution: Introduces the notion of circular homomorphisms between digraphs as the natural framework in which this conjecture is formulated, and develops the theory of circular $F$-colourability (Section 2) that underpins the conjecture.
paper_title: On the Complexity of Digraph Colourings and Vertex Arboricity

title: Problem 5.40
statement_text: For given $k,b\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k\geq b$, is there a directed graph $\vec{K}(k,b)$ with vertex set $\binom{[k]}{b}$ such that the following holds? The subdigraph of $\vec{K}(k,b)$ induced by any $\{B_{1},\ldots,B_{l}\}\subseteq\binom{[k]}{b}$ is acylic if and only if $\bigcap_{i=1}^{l}{B_{i}}\neq\emptyset$.
context_text: Digraphs are loopless but may have parallel and anti-parallel arcs; a digon is a directed cycle of length two, and a vertex set is acyclic if it induces an acyclic subdigraph. A $b$-tuple $k$-colouring of a digraph $D$ assigns to each vertex a set of $b$ colours from $[k]=\{1,\dots,k\}$ so that, for each colour $i$, the vertices whose set contains $i$ induce an acyclic subdigraph; the fractional dichromatic number of $D$ is the minimum $k/b$ for which a $b$-tuple $k$-colouring exists. For graphs, a $(k,b)$-colouring (sets of $b$ colours, disjoint on adjacent vertices) exists if and only if there is a homomorphism to the Kneser graph $K(k,b)$. A circular homomorphism from $D_1$ to $D_2$ is a map whose preimages of acyclic sets are acyclic. If a digraph $\vec{K}(k,b)$ as in the problem exists, then $D$ is $b$-tuple $k$-colourable if and only if there is a circular homomorphism from $D$ to $\vec{K}(k,b)$, a directed analogue of the Kneser graph reformulation. For $k=b+1$ such a digraph exists: the directed cycle of length $b+1$ on the sets $[b+1]\setminus\{i\}$.
paper_title: On the Complexity of Digraph Colourings and Vertex Arboricity
